title: JavaScript Performance Optimization Core Check
description: Check your understanding of measuring performance, browser rendering, long tasks, DOM batching, debouncing, throttling, memoization, lazy loading, workers, network cost, and DevTools profiling.
author: DailyCoder

questions.prompt: What is the best first step before optimizing JavaScript code?

options.text: Measure the problem and identify the real bottleneck

questions.explanation: Optimization should start with measurement so you improve the code that is actually causing user-visible problems.

questions.prompt: Which API is designed for precise timing measurements in the browser?
questions.explanation: `performance.now()` provides high-resolution timing useful for performance measurements.

questions.prompt: Why can heavy JavaScript make a page feel frozen?

options.text: It can keep the main thread busy, delaying input and rendering
HTML stops existing while JavaScript runs

questions.explanation: Most browser JavaScript runs on the main thread, which also handles many interaction and rendering tasks.

questions.prompt: A long task is commonly described as main-thread work that takes more than about how long?
questions.explanation: The 50 millisecond threshold is commonly used as a warning line for long main-thread tasks.

questions.prompt: What is layout in browser rendering?

options.text: Calculating the size and position of elements

questions.explanation: Layout is the browser's process of determining where elements go and how large they are.

options.text: Waits until activity pauses before running a function
Runs a function on every animation frame forever

questions.explanation: Debouncing resets a timer on repeated calls and runs the callback after activity has paused.

options.text: Limits a function to run at most once during a time window
Runs a function only after page reload

questions.explanation: Throttling controls the rate of repeated function calls while activity continues.

options.text: When an expensive function receives the same inputs repeatedly
When every input is unique and the function is cheap
When the function depends on random values
When memory usage must always be zero

questions.explanation: Memoization avoids repeated expensive work by returning cached results for repeated inputs.

options.text: Loading a module when it is needed

questions.explanation: Dynamic `import()` returns a Promise and can defer loading module code until the feature is needed.

questions.prompt: Which API is usually best for JavaScript-driven visual updates before the next paint?
questions.explanation: `requestAnimationFrame()` schedules visual work to run before the browser's next paint.

questions.prompt: What are Web Workers mainly useful for?

options.text: Running CPU-heavy work off the main thread
Directly editing DOM elements from another file

questions.explanation: Workers can run JavaScript on a background thread, but they cannot directly access the DOM.

questions.prompt: Which DevTools panel is most useful for recording main-thread work during a slow interaction?
questions.explanation: The Performance panel records JavaScript execution, rendering work, long tasks, and event handlers.
